basics.name: Gonzalo Cruz Gómez
basics.label: Data & AI Engineer
basics.summary: Final-year Data Science & Engineering student at URJC (graduating June 2027), currently on Repsol's Data Intelligence Platform team. Builds data systems end to end: orchestration, streaming, and models that hold up on real data. Founder of Asociación Datalab. Three years of Telecommunications Engineering at UC3M before switching to data.

work.name: Repsol
work.summary: Talent Energy internship on the Data Intelligence Platform team at Repsol's Madrid Campus, running in parallel with the final year of the degree.

work.name: Asociación Datalab
work.summary: Started the association because project-driven learning didn't exist at the university yet.
highlights: Handled legal registration and defined the strategic roadmap from zero.
Organised technical workshops and coordinated the first collaborative data projects.

work.name: Self-employed
work.summary: Tutored high-school students through calculus, linear algebra, mechanics and electromagnetism, including Selectividad preparation.
highlights: 100% pass rate over five years; 90% of students improved by at least three grade points.
Built individual study plans per student rather than a shared syllabus.

projects.name: TripAdvisor Restaurants Pipeline
projects.description: Full-stack data system over European restaurant data: a five-task Airflow DAG for ETL plus ML plus streaming, a distributed clustering stage, and a web app on top.
highlights: Orchestrated a five-task Airflow DAG over 1M+ rows in 50k-row chunks — extract, clean, EDA, preprocess (normalisation, OHE or label encoding by cardinality, incremental PCA), stream to Kafka — so the pipeline stays memory-safe on a laptop.
Applied PySpark ML KMeans with automatic K selection via silhouette scoring (K = 10–80); every parameter (chunk size, thresholds, Kafka config) lives in one config.toml read at runtime.
Built two Spark Structured Streaming consumers — a fast filter path and an ML-scored path computing centroid distances — writing timestamped classifications in real time.
Shipped a FastAPI + React/Vite app: restaurant search by cosine similarity within clusters, plus a live scoring tab pushing classifications to the browser over Server-Sent Events.
Streamed to Kafka with a fault-tolerant producer (acks=all, sub-batch delivery).

projects.name: Stroke Risk Prediction
projects.description: Binary classification of stroke risk on 5,110 patients at roughly 5% positive rate, where a false negative costs far more than a false positive.
highlights: Optimised for recall over accuracy and moved the decision threshold explicitly, since the clinical cost of a missed stroke dominates the cost of a false alarm.
Rebalanced with SMOTE and selected features with RFECV rather than hand-picking.
Benchmarked an MLP against a logistic-regression baseline (0.88 recall, 0.84 AUC); kept AUC-ROC and F1 as the reported metrics.

projects.name: Real-Time Hashtag Trending
projects.description: Continuous ranking of trending hashtags over a live tweet feed, using Spark DStreams and a five-minute sliding window.
highlights: Filtered to US-only tweets before aggregation to keep the ranking meaningful instead of dominated by non-English noise.
Implemented the window with a reduceByKeyAndWindow inverse function, so each slide costs the interval rather than the whole window.

projects.name: Hadoop Sentiment Analysis
projects.description: AFINN-111 sentiment scoring over a 314MB Twitter corpus on a cluster built from scratch rather than borrowed.
highlights: Stood up HDFS and YARN across containers with Docker Compose, including the deploy script, instead of using a pre-built image.
Wrote the MapReduce job to score each tweet against the AFINN-111 lexicon and aggregate by term.

projects.name: Forest Fire Spread Prediction
projects.description: Predicting burned area in Montesinho Natural Park from meteorological covariates, on data that is zero-inflated and heavily right-skewed — the case where OLS quietly fails.
highlights: Compared GLM and GAM fits by cross-validated RMSE; GAMs won because the covariate effects are not linear.
Handled high skew, missing values and near-zero-variance predictors with log transforms, imputation and feature selection before modelling.

projects.name: Bank Customer Churn
projects.description: Churn prediction on 10,000 customers with Naive Bayes, AdaBoost and K-NN implemented from the maths in base R, then compared against library versions.
highlights: Reimplemented each algorithm from its mathematical definition to check understanding, then compared against the off-the-shelf implementation.
The from-scratch Naive Bayes reached 34.55% recall against the library's 23.24% — the gap came from how smoothing was handled on rare categories.

projects.name: Cross-Lingual Sentiment Study
projects.description: Ongoing study of cross-lingual sentiment transfer between Spanish and English with XLM-R, focused on evaluation rather than headline F1.
highlights: Building the evaluation harness first: per-language slices, label-distribution shifts and error analysis instead of a single aggregate score.
Fine-tuning on a 4GB-VRAM GPU, which forces explicit choices about batch size, gradient accumulation and fp16.

projects.name: Final Degree Thesis — ANN over multimodal data
projects.description: Final degree thesis on approximate nearest-neighbour search over multimodal data, on an existing algorithm owned by the advising group. Definitive title pending.
highlights: First phase is a codebase audit and profiling of the existing implementation, not a rewrite.
Rebuilding parts of it in Polars, with MLflow for experiment tracking and Airflow for the benchmark runs.

projects.name: Time Series Analysis with SARIMA
projects.description: Four series forecast following Box-Jenkins — identify, estimate, diagnose, repeat — with grid search, Fourier terms and temporal windowing.

projects.name: Whitehead Sample Size Analysis
projects.description: Minimum n to detect a deviation from p₀ = 0.003, comparing Score Test, exact binomial and Wilcoxon at the edge of their validity.

projects.name: Dual-Mode RC Robot
projects.description: STM32 Nucleo-L152RE vehicle with autonomous ultrasonic avoidance or manual Bluetooth control, on interrupt-driven firmware (TIM2 capture, TIM3 PWM).
